items.title: Two rescued as building collapses in Kubwa
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Two residents trapped in the rubble of a collapsed one-storey building at Kubwa 2/2, near Yellow Page, have been successfully rescued and are currently receiving treatment at the Kubwa General Hospital, where they remain in stable condition. Head of Media and Public Relations at the Federal Capital Territory Emergency Management Department FEMD, Nkechi Isa, who confirmed this in a statement said the victims were trapped on the ground floor of the residential property when the right segment of the structure collapsed at approximately 11:30am on Friday. According to Isa, the affected building comprises six blocks of flats, and other occupants of the property were out at the time of the incident, a development that helped limit the number of persons caught up in the collapse. She said the FEMD received a distress call at 11:38am and swiftly mobilised to the scene to extract the trapped victims. While the two residents were pulled out alive without fatalities, the collapse resulted in significant loss of personal belongings and household items, she added. Isa said the Department of Development Control and the FCT Police Command also responded to the incident to secure the area and initiate investigations into the structural failure. The post Two rescued as building collapses in Kubwa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bassitenga : la communauté musulmane appelée à s’inspirer des enseignements du prophète Mohamed
items.description: Bassitenga : la communauté musulmane appelée à s'inspirer des enseignements du prophète Mohamed Ziniaré, 26 août 2026 (AIB)-La communauté musulmane de la province du Bassitenga a célébré, dans la nuit du 25 au 26 août 2026 à la grande mosquée de Ziniaré, le Mouloud, commémorant la naissance du prophète Mohamed. Organisée par le bureau provincial de l'Association de la communauté musulmane du Bassitenga, la cérémonie a réuni de nombreux fidèles et responsables religieux autour de prières, de lectures coraniques et de prêches consacrés à la vie et aux enseignements du prophète. Les prédicateurs ont invité les participants à faire de Mohamed un modèle dans leur conduite quotidienne, en mettant l'accent sur le respect, la solidarité, la tolérance et la bonne moralité. S'exprimant au nom du camarade Yacouba Dialla, président provincial de la communauté musulmane, l'imam cheikh Saidou Tapsoba a appelé les fidèles à préserver leur unité et à privilégier le respect et le dialogue. « Si nous nous unissons, cela rendrait agréable notre vie et notre pratique religieuse. Le président demande à ce qu'on se respecte, qu'on évite les querelles et qu'on parle d'une seule voix dans notre province », a-t-il déclaré. La cérémonie a également connu la participation du haut-commissaire de la province, El Hadj Saidou Guigma. Au nom des autorités, il a salué la contribution de la communauté musulmane à la paix et au vivre-ensemble. « Nous sommes venus au nom du camarade Ibrahim Traoré, au nom du gouvernement et au nom de la camarade gouverneure pour apporter notre soutien à la communauté musulmane et la remercier pour les efforts consentis dans le cadre du vivre-ensemble », a-t-il indiqué. Le haut-commissaire a exhorté les fidèles à soutenir la dynamique de la Révolution progressiste populaire et à œuvrer à la cohésion sociale et à la construction nationale. Agence d'information du Burkina LC/ata

items.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s Hasan Piker Problem
items.description: T he hard-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker warned Jewish Americans last week that their excessive identification with Israel would subject them to anti-Semitic attacks. “If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action—not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews,” he said. Piker’s tone was one of rueful concern, not unlike the pose adopted by anti-Semites throughout history. “No person with a sense of the dignity of mankind can condone the persecution of the Jewish race in Germany. But no person of honesty and vision can look on their pro-war policy here today without seeing the dangers involved in such a policy both for us and for them,” the Nazi sympathizer Charles Lindbergh said in 1941. Several leading Democrats, including Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan and House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries, issued statements denouncing Piker’s ugly warning to the Jews as a barely veiled anti-Semitic threat. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat running for Michigan’s other Senate seat, trod more carefully. He issued a statement “in response to Hasan Piker’s comments” affirming that “all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence” and denouncing anti-Semitism, but the statement itself did not say whether Piker’s comment qualified as anti-Semitism. El-Sayed instead dismissed Piker as a distraction, saying at a recent rally, “The effort to make this race about a streamer in L.A. is actually kind of laughable.” Most Democrats followed El-Sayed’s line that Piker was irrelevant. “This election is about what’s going to happen when we elect Abdul to the United States Senate. I am done, so don’t any reporter ask me again about Hasan Piker. It’s not what November is about,” Representative Debbie Dingell said at a rally for El-Sayed. [ Graeme Wood: Something is happening to America’s moral code ] Democrats have good reason to say this. El-Sayed is running a close race to hold a seat that Democrats probably need to retain to win control of the Senate in the midterm elections. But the truth is that Piker, and the uncomfortable questions raised by his alliance with El-Sayed, is one of the important questions at stake in the election. If Piker were just an internet pundit, his rant—the latest entry in a long list of outrageous comments he has made—would be of little consequence to the Democratic Party. Piker has said that “America deserved 9/11,” praised Mao Zedong as “one of the great leaders of this world,” and mourned the collapse of the Soviet Union as “one of the greatest catastrophes of the 20th century.” His ideology is profoundly authoritarian . But several left-wing Democrats, especially El-Sayed, have campaigned with Piker and elevated him into one of their most prominent surrogates. So El-Sayed’s alliance with Piker has become a political and moral crisis. In Michigan, Democrats are trying to avoid handing Republicans their first Senate win in the state in more than three decades. But if El-Sayed wins, he would throw open the doors of the party to a strain of militant politics that many Jews justifiably consider dangerous. The Democratic Party is now divided between those who are trying to force El-Sayed to stop encouraging left-wing anti-Semites and those who give him their unconditional support. T he Michigan Senate election has presented liberals with a grim choice. The Republican candidate, Mike Rogers, has pledged support for a corrupt, racist, authoritarian-minded administration. Rogers hasn’t made even the tiniest concession to Donald Trump critics. But supporting El-Sayed means accepting a strain of anti-Semitic politics that to date has had no place within the Democratic Party. What’s more, El-Sayed has already said that he intends to use his victory as a platform to reshape the party. Him winning could invite a future in which the United States has not just one party that is open to bigots but two. Although El-Sayed has never said anything nearly as inflammatory as the sorts of comments Piker makes routinely, his mixture of anti-Zionism and populism treats pro-Israel activism as a nefarious and all-pervasive force . He has denied that any Democrat who believes in human rights could have any motive other than money for holding a position on Israel different from the one he prefers. El-Sayed tends to depict nearly all opposition to his candidacy as financially driven, but when applied to Jewish political activity, this charge becomes even more conspiratorial. Ann Arbor, where El-Sayed lives, is home to a branch of the Free Palestine movement that has engaged in violent intimidation of Jewish Democrats. Activists at the University of Michigan not only seized the central campus grounds for their own but also vandalized the business of Jordan Acker, a Democratic regent, and made middle-of-the-night attacks on his home, one of which involved shattering his window with a jar of urine. El-Sayed has campaigned on the Michigan campus with Amir Makled, a lawyer who defended the protesters and who has shared anti-Semitic and pro-Hezbollah social-media posts. When the Justice Department charged eight of the protesters—one of whom had worked on El-Sayed’s campaign—in a plot to commit still more acts of intimidation, El-Sayed treated the indictment as biased, telling reporters, “It’s a lot more about what you’re advocating for that gets you indicted or not indicted, rather than what you did.” Dana Nessel, the state’s attorney general, has faced anti-Semitic harassment and has said that she plans to skip the state party’s August convention rather than endure more abuse. At the party’s April nominating caucus, Mallory McMorrow, a then-candidate for Senate, reported that her Jewish husband was subjected to an anti-Semitic slur. On the weekend before the primary, Walter Masterson, a left-wing streamer who has appeared with El-Sayed, disrupted an event for Haley Stevens, El-Sayed’s pro-Israel opponent in the Democratic primary, forcing the brewery hosting it to cancel the event. El-Sayed did not condemn the bully-boy tactics used on his behalf. Before he warned American Jews that they were bringing anti-Semitism on themselves by identifying with Israel, Piker displayed on his Twitch stream a quote attributed to Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee for Congress in a suburban Detroit district: “The entire purpose of my campaign is to make sure America continues to support Israel. I don’t think it’s wrong for Jews in America to want to put Israel first. America is not our homeland and we have been victims of antisemitism here.” Moss insists that the quote is a pure fabrication, and no one has yet produced any evidence of its authenticity. Numerous Democrats denounced Piker’s comments. Instead of apologizing, though, Piker replied on X , “Aipac boss call was made,” implying that only the influence of the pro-Israel lobby could have caused Democrats to object to his rhetoric. [ James Loeffler: The hatred that broke American politics ] El-Sayed has refused pleas from his fellow Democrats to break off his alliance with Piker, who joined him at a pool party on the last day of campaigning before the primary. El-Sayed first brushed off the requests by likening Piker to Joe Rogan, a controversial podcaster whose show some Democrats have appeared on (but not a figure they have brought out on the campaign trail). More recently, he argued that the demands that he distance himself from Piker come from “cancel culture that all of us agreed was a bad idea back in 2020, but we seem to want to bring it back.” This is a dodge. El-Sayed’s fellow Democrats are not trying to silence or punish Piker. They are asking El-Sayed, who chose to bring Piker out to campaign for and endorse him, to make clear where he stands. “Abdul El-Sayed had a prime opportunity to cut ties with Piker and directly disavow his words, but he did not,” Democratic Representative Hillary Scholten of Michigan told Politico . “There is a lot of work left to do to unite the party.” Notably, El-Sayed is using an evasive construction similar to the one that J. D. Vance has employed to justify his friendship with Tucker Carlson. “We have far more important work to do than canceling each other,” the vice president told a conservative gathering last year. The reason Vance uses this deflection is obvious. He wishes to benefit from Carlson’s support without being held responsible for his ally’s most inflammatory claims. This has set off a bitter struggle within the right. Some Republicans are trying to throw Carlson out of the coalition; Vance wants to keep him in. Democrats have little trouble understanding that the right-wing infighting over Carlson is about whether the Republican tent, which already includes racists, nativists, and vicious Islamophobes, is also big enough to include anti-Semites. They have correspondingly little trouble making harsh judgments about the moral compromises Republicans are contemplating in the process. What many Democrats don’t wish to admit is that they are entertaining a similar choice themselves. El-Sayed and Piker have professed their abhorrence of anti-Semitism. But so has Vance—and, so, for that matter, has Carlson. If your opposition to anti-Semitism applies only to your ideological adversaries, and you excuse or ignore it from your allies, it is an empty bromide. When Democrats dismiss the controversy over Piker and the movement he stands for, they are treating the growing influence of left-wing anti-Semitism as unworthy of concern—or, worse still, a fait accompli. The Democrats imploring El-Sayed to renounce Piker want more than a generalized promise to safeguard Jewish safety, or a statement that “nobody” speaks for the candidate. They are seeking some assurance from El-Sayed that he will speak out in opposition to attacks against Jews by his own supporters. El-Sayed has responded as if the only reason Democrats might hesitate to endorse him is that they hold a personal grudge against him. “There are a few people who are still nursing wounds or grievances from the primary,” he told Semafor . “I get it. Losing is hard.” It is true that losing elections is hard. Losing your moral principles, on the other hand, can be surprisingly easy.

items.title: Northshore Apparel shows what 24-hour economy can deliver – Mahama
items.description: President John Mahama has cited the Northshore Apparel Hub as an example of how his government’s 24-hour economy initiative is expected to create jobs, increase production and accelerate Ghana’s exports. Speaking at the opening of the Northshore Apparel Hub, the President said the company’s plans to operate multiple shifts would create more employment opportunities for young people while increasing production for export. “This is an example of what our vision, the 24-hour economy initiative, is meant to do,” President Mahama said. He said Northshore was expected to run several shifts, allowing the company to employ more workers and increase its output. “North Shore is going to run several shifts, and it means that several more young people will get jobs to do,” he said. According to the President, Northshore is part of a wider wave of factories and businesses expected to adopt multiple shifts under the 24-hour economy initiative. “And it is not only North Shore, there are several other factories that are coming up that are going to run multiple shifts and create businesses for our people,” he said. He said the initiative had two key objectives: creating jobs and increasing Ghana’s export earnings. “And so the 24-hour economy is designed to achieve the creation of jobs and accelerated exports,” he said. President Mahama said the apparel hub was already contributing to those objectives, having created at least 2,000 jobs. “And North Shore certifies both because it has created at least 2,000 jobs already and the bulk of its products are going to be exported to bring foreign exchange into Ghana,” he said. He said the company’s export-oriented operations would help Ghana earn much-needed foreign exchange while creating employment opportunities locally. The President also said Northshore had been registered under the Free Zones regime, allowing it to benefit from incentives available to businesses operating under the programme. “North Shore is registered under the Free Zones, and so it will benefit from all the incentives that the Free Zones has to offer,” he said. President Mahama said Northshore would also benefit from tax incentives available to manufacturers that locate in rural and northern parts of the country. He explained that the current tax regime provided lower tax rates for manufacturers that established operations in rural areas and the northern parts of Ghana. “Apart from that, it will also have tax incentives because the current tax regime gives a lower tax rate to manufacturers who go to rural areas and also to manufacturers who locate in the northern part of Ghana,” he said. He added that companies such as Northshore would receive duty and tax exemptions on plants and equipment. “They will also receive duty and tax exemptions on plants and equipment,” he said. The President said the company had indicated its intention to proceed with a second phase of development, which would allow it to benefit from further exemptions. “A large new regime has already said they have intentions of continuing the second phase. And so in the second phase, they will enjoy the exemptions from duties and taxes that they deserve,” he said. President Mahama also announced plans for government to introduce a net-metering framework that would allow companies with solar power plants to supply excess electricity to the national grid. He said Parliament would be asked to pass legislation to establish the system. “Apart from that, we are going to get Parliament to pass a net metering bill,” he said. The proposed system would be particularly useful to companies such as Northshore that generate part of their electricity through solar power. Under net metering, the President explained, excess electricity generated by a company’s solar plant could be fed into the national grid, with a meter recording the amount supplied. “That will allow companies like North Shore that have their solar plants to net meter with the electricity company or NETCO so that if they are producing more than they need from their solar plants, it will be integrated into the national grid and there will be a meter that calculates how much they are owed,” he said. He said companies would then be compensated for electricity supplied to the grid. “And so if they are owed, it means NETCO has to pay them,” he said. On the other hand, companies that consume more electricity than they generate would be required to pay the difference. “And if they consume more, then they will have to pay NETCO the difference between their power. They call it net metering,” he explained. He said the government intended to introduce the system soon. “And so we are going to introduce net metering in the country soon,” President Mahama said.

items.title: ‘Do I look 80?’ – Atiku dismisses age concerns ahead of presidential election
items.description: The African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, said he is fit and healthy, dismissing age concerns ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Read Also: Gunmen kill APC chairman in Kogi, abduct one “Do I look to you like someone who has reached 80 years of age?” he asked the BBC Hausa interviewer. He had been asked if his age would not affect his ability to provide effective leadership if elected. The interviewer noted that Atiku would be “almost or nearly 80 years old” by the time Nigerians vote in 2027, and asked what he would say to those who considered him too old. He responded: “You went and voted for someone who is 80, I mean 90 years old. How old is President Bola, 90?” When the interviewer corrected him, saying Tinubu was not yet 80, Atiku responded, “Do I look to you like someone who has reached 80 years of age?” On opposition Also, Atiku said it was wrong to claim he had become an obstacle to the opposition coalition. “That is a baseless accusation levelled against me. I was actually the one who initiated the coalition. Nobody else. I, Atiku Abubakar, started it,” he said. He added that Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, are the two major opposition figures who had left the group. “It was just Kwankwaso… he was with us at first, then he left. “Yes, and also Peter Obi. It’s just them, but the rest of us are still here continuing our work.” Atiku expressed optimism that they would all still work together for the good of the country. Vanguard News The post ‘Do I look 80?’ – Atiku dismisses age concerns ahead of presidential election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: From refuse dump site to garment factory – CEO tells Northshore Apparel’s transformation story
items.description: What was once an abandoned latrine pit and refuse dump has been transformed into a modern garment manufacturing facility by Northshore Apparel, in a development described as a symbol of hope and economic opportunity. The Chief Executive Officer of Northshore Apparel, Nurideen Mohammed, said the land on which the factory now stands was previously an abandoned latrine pit that had been turned into a refuse dump. “Not long ago, the earth beneath our feet was an abandoned latrine pit, and that had been turned into a refuse dam,” Nurideen Mohammed said. “It was where this town sent what it no longer wanted. Today, it is a harbour of hope.” Speaking at the launch of the Northshore Apparel Hub as part of 24-Hour Economy Facility, on August 28, Northshore Apparel CEO said the transformation of the site reflects the broader vision behind the company’s investment in Northern Ghana. Mr Mohammed said the facility demonstrates that places and people often considered to have little value can be transformed when given the right investment and opportunities. “What was once a receiver now produces goods worn in New York and Frankfurt,” he said. He said the transformation was not merely about constructing a factory but about creating a new economic identity for the community. “What was called trouble is now called talent, and it clocks in every morning at 7,” Nurideen Mohammed said. ‘Nothing and no one is beyond redemption’ The Northshore Apparel CEO said the company believes that no piece of land, region or individual should be permanently written off. “We believe that nothing and no one is beyond redemption,” he said. “Not a piece of land, not a region, not a young person whom the world has already written off.” Nurideen Mohammed said the transformation of the site should also inspire a similar transformation in the lives of young people who lack opportunities. “If a pit can become a factory, then a boy loitering by the roadside can become a machinist, a supervisor, and a plant manager,” he said. From waste site to centre of production Mr Mohammed said the development represents what can be achieved when private investment, financing, traditional authorities, development partners and local communities work together. He acknowledged the contribution of the company’s board, financiers, development partners, traditional authorities and workers to the establishment of the facility. The Northshore Apparel facility is designed to manufacture garments for international and regional markets while creating employment opportunities for people in surrounding communities. Mr Mohammed said the transformation of the former refuse site into an export-oriented manufacturing facility should serve as a reminder that neglected spaces can be converted into productive centres of economic activity. “Today, it is a harbour of hope,” Mr Mohammed said.

items.title: Meurtre sauvage d’un enfant de 5 ans à Blida : la Gendarmerie élucide l’affaire
items.description: Un garçon de 5 ans a été retrouvé mort et mutilé dans la forêt de Bouinan à Blida lundi 23 août dernier. Cinq jours après, quatre suspects ont été arrêtés, annonce la Gendarmerie nationale ce vendredi 28 août. La nouvelle avait bouleversé les Algériens. Tout a commencé avec la réception par la brigade de gendarmerie de Chebli dans la même wilaya d’un signalement sur la disparition de l’enfant. Le même jour, les gendarmes sont informés de la présence d’un corps calciné au lieu-dit Laayoune. Les gendarmes, accompagnés des éléments de la police scientifique se rendent sur les lieux, et l’identité de la victime est déterminée. Meurtre d’un enfant de 5 ans à Blida : quatre arrestations, le principal suspect court toujours Deux jours après cette découverte macabre, la Gendarmerie publie sur les réseaux sociaux la photo du principal suspect de ce crime abject et lancé un appel à témoin. Ce vendredi, elle annonce avoir réussi à élucider les circonstances de ce crime qui a plongé la région de Blida et toute l’Algérie dans l’effroi. « Après l’intensification des recherches et l’exploitation de toutes les données, l’identité des suspects a été déterminée », a indiqué la Gendarmerie ce vendredi dans une vidéo postée sur Facebook. Au total, quatre suspects ont été arrêtés alors que le « principal suspect est toujours en fuite », a ajouté la Gendarmerie en précisant que deux voitures et une moto, utilisées pour commettre ce crime, ont été saisies. Il reste le mobile du crime qui n’a pas été dévoilé. L’article Meurtre sauvage d’un enfant de 5 ans à Blida : la Gendarmerie élucide l’affaire est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: SOUM/DJIBO : L’Immersion patriotique obligatoire 2026 s’achève sur une note de fierté et d’engagement
items.description: SOUM/DJIBO : L’Immersion patriotique obligatoire 2026 s’achève sur une note de fierté et d’engagement Djibo, 27 août 2026 (AIB) – La session 2026 de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire a pris fin jeudi 27 août 2026 à Djibo, au cours d’une cérémonie présidée par le Camarade Haut-Commissaire de la province du Soum, Wend Nere Wilfried TOUGMA, président de la cellule provinciale de l’Immersion patriotique, en présence du Camarade Commandant du 22ᵉ Bataillon d’Intervention Rapide (22ᵉ BIR), vice-président de ladite cellule. L’événement a réuni les autorités administratives, coutumières et religieuses, les responsables des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), ainsi que des parents d’élèves et des citoyens de Djibo. La montée solennelle des couleurs nationales a ouvert la cérémonie, suivie de démonstrations de self-défense exécutées par les jeunes et d’un défilé au pas, sous les applaudissements de l’assistance. Prenant la parole au nom de ses camarades, la représentante des appelés, Kadiata Tamboura, a exprimé leur reconnaissance aux autorités, aux encadreurs et à la population pour leur accompagnement tout au long de la formation. Elle a notamment souligné que, si l’immersion patriotique prend fin, « le combat pour la Nation, lui, continue ». Le Camarade Haut-Commissaire Wend Néré Wilfried TOUGMA a salué la détermination des jeunes et la qualité de leurs prestations. Il a également remercié les cadres, les autorités coutumières et religieuses, la population de Djibo ainsi que les donateurs ayant contribué à la réussite de l’initiative. S’adressant aux appelés, il les a exhortés à mettre en pratique les valeurs civiques et morales acquises durant leur formation. « Conservez précieusement toutes les valeurs civiques et morales acquises et utilisez-les à bon escient. Soyez au quotidien le rempart inébranlable du patriotisme, de la discipline et de la souveraineté de notre Nation ! », a-t-il déclaré. La remise des attributs civiques aux appelés a constitué l’un des temps forts de la rencontre. Grâce à la contribution de donateurs venus renforcer la dotation initiale de la coordination nationale « Nafona », chaque appelé a reçu trois exemplaires du Manifeste de la Révolution. Dans le même esprit de soutien à la jeunesse, la population civile avait également offert des cartes d’identité biométriques de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (CIB-AES) à l’ensemble des appelés de la province au cours de leur immersion. La cérémonie s’est achevée dans une ambiance de fierté et de satisfaction. Parents, autorités et citoyens ont salué la discipline et la maturité démontrées par les jeunes à l’issue de cette expérience. Agence d'information du Burkina AG/ata

items.title: PML-N's Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani sworn in as new AJK prime minister
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani was sworn in as Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s prime minister on Friday. Gillani took oath at a televised ceremony, where he expressed gratitude to PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and the party’s senior leadership. Addressing the gathering, the newly elected prime minister said he was thankful for the leadership’s “affection and faith” in him and pledged to uphold that trust. “I am thankful for the leadership and party’s affection and faith in me, and I assure you that even if I have to work day and night, I will uphold this faith,” Gillani said. He urged members of the Legislative Assembly to cooperate with him, stressing that “we must move forward together and build an AJK that is exemplary for the whole world”. “Ours is a small region,” Gillani said, noting that “similar to the rest of the country, AJK also has governance issues and unemployment”. “Why does anyone work in this country? It is so they can put food on the table, give their children a better education and afford to pay hospital bills,” he said, stressing that the three points were “the basis on which his government will move forward”. He emphasised that the youth must be provided employment opportunities. “We have to take all possible efforts to ensure employment for the youth so they may not be led astray and continue on a path to a brighter future”. Gillani stated that the hospitals in the region also needed improvement. “If we address these three things to even a minor extent, many of our tensions will be resolved.” He expressed confidence that the PML-N majority in the legislative assembly will “utilise the experience of senior members and energy of the youth in their ranks”. “I am confident that at the end of our tenure, AJK’s prosperity and development will be used as an example all over Pakistan,” he hoped. Gillani was elected as PM after securing 30 of the 44 votes polled in the assembly earlier in the day. His sole contender was PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who bagged 14 votes in the contest for the top office. The AJK Assembly comprises 53 members, but its present strength is 46 — PML-N’s being 32, including its allies, and PPP’s 14 — because elections to seven seats in Poonch and Sudhnoti districts have yet to be held. However, 44 votes were polled in Friday’s elections as the speaker did not cast his vote and PML-N regional president Shah Ghulam Qadir was not present in the assembly. Qadir, along with former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, had previously opposed Gillani’s nomination for the post. However, when assembly proceedings began on Friday, Haider entered the House alongside Gillani. After the votes were counted, Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq announced the result, declaring Gillani as the winner amid clapping and slogans from the galleries. Gillani has succeeded PPP’s Rathore, who was elected as the prime minister in November 2025. Following his election, PM Shehbaz congratulated him and expressed hope that he would “play an effective role in the development of AJK and the welfare of its people”, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported . Citing an official statement, the report said PM Shehbaz credited PML-N leadership and workers’ “hard work” for the party’s victory in AJK. He said the federal government would continue extending all possible support for the development, prosperity and improved living standards of the people of AJK and termed the “continuation of the democratic process in Azad Jammu and Kashmir a welcome development”. Gillani’s nomination PML-N’s decision to nominate Gillani was announced by PM Shehbaz at a meeting with four senior PML-N leaders from AJK in Islamabad, late on Wednesday night. The meeting, which took place at the Prime Min­ister’s House, was attended by PML-N AJK President Shah Ghulam Qadir, his predecessor and former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, the party’s regional secretary general and asse­mbly speaker, Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, and Deputy Spe­a­ker Ahmed Raza Qadri. The prime minister was accompanied by his aide, Rana Sanaullah, and senior PML-N leader Saad Rafique. Gillani was also invited to the PM House but did not join the meeting, where PM Shehbaz infor­med the visiting leaders that party supremo Nawaz Sharif had decided to nominate Gillani as the party’s candidate for the AJK premiership. The decision, however, triggered a sharp reaction from Qadir and Haider, who reportedly expressed their disagreement and announced that they would not participate in Friday’s election process. However, only Qadir did not participate in the election. Speculation that Gillani could be chosen for the premiership had been rife since he was elected to the assembly on a reserved seat on Aug 24. However, the party’s regional leadership believed that the formula followed in 2016, when Haider was elevated as prime minister, would be repeated this time as well. Following the reaction of the two senior leaders, Sanaullah and Rafique held another meeting with them, but it remained inconclusive, sources told Dawn. In a post-midnight message on X, Qadir assured the “self-respecting people of Azad Kashmir” that he would not compromise on their honour and dignity. “Nawaz Sharif’s slogan of giving respect to the vote will be ensured,” he added. On Thursday afternoon, however, PML-N central information secretary and Punjab senior minister Marriyum Aurangzeb posted on X that PM Shehbaz had finalised Gillani as the party’s candidate and directed him to submit his nomination papers for election as AJK prime minister. AJK polls The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10. Meanwhile, the third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N . As for the reserved seats, the PML-N has bagged six and the PPP two. The PPP has alleged widespread rigging and irregularities in the elections.

items.title: Sanguié/Pouni : JB-Tech choisit la voie de l’entrepreneuriat à Pouni
items.description: BURKINA-SANGUIE-POUNI-ENTREPRENEURIAT Sanguié/Pouni : JB-Tech choisit la voie de l'entrepreneuriat à Pouni Pouni, 28 août 2026 (AIB) – Titulaire d’une licence en biologie générale, Boubou Jean-Baptiste Tiené, alias JB-Tech, a choisi de tourner le dos au chômage en s'installant à Pouni pour entreprendre. Plutôt que d'attendre un emploi dans la Fonction publique, ce jeune diplômé s'est lancé avec succès dans l'entrepreneuriat. Dans son atelier, il s'est spécialisé dans la sérigraphie, réalisant des impressions sur T-shirts, des bâches et des affiches. Cette activité principale est complétée par une boutique de vente de prêt-à-porter, de parfums et de chaussures, lui permettant de diversifier ses revenus et de subvenir aux besoins de sa famille. Fidèle à sa vision de l'autonomisation de la jeunesse, JB-Tech ne se limite pas à la production. Il partage déjà son savoir-faire avec deux jeunes scolaires venus apprendre le métier à ses côtés. « Avec un petit coup de pouce en équipement, je pourrai mieux m’équiper et employer beaucoup plus de jeunes déscolarisés de Pouni », confie-t-il, convaincu que l'entrepreneuriat constitue une alternative efficace face au chômage. Le parcours de Jean-Baptiste Tiené illustre l'engagement de cette nouvelle génération d'entrepreneurs burkinabè qui transforment leur localité en un véritable pôle d'initiatives économiques. Agence d'information du Burkina JS/PB/AS/ATA

items.title: AG inaugurates 11-member committee to implement Ghana’s proposed constitutional reforms
items.description: Attorney General (AG) and Minister of Justice, Dr Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, has inaugurated an 11-member Constitution Review Implementation Committee (CRIC) to begin work on proposals for the review of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution. The inauguration follows the government’s release of its position paper on recommendations contained in the report of the Constitution Review Committee chaired by Professor H. Kwesi Prempeh. The new committee has been tasked with examining the government’s position paper alongside the recommendations of the Constitution Review Committee and developing a comprehensive framework for implementing the proposals. Presidential Legal Counsel and former Attorney General and Minister of Justice, Marietta Brew Appiah-Oppong, chairs the committee. The other members are Dr Justice Srem Sai, Thomas Ampem Nyarko, Charlotte Osei, Dr Rainer Akumperigya, Emelia Ankomah, Kwame Ayimadu Antwi, Samuel Passah, Oliver Baker Vormawor, Salamatu Iliasu and Eric Owusu-Mensa. Emelia Ankomah represents the Majority in Parliament, while Kwame Ayimadu Antwi represents the Minority. Samuel Passah represents local government, and Eric Owusu-Mensa serves as Parliament’s representative. Oliver Baker Vormawor is the Secretary, while Salamatu Iliasu serves as the Draftsperson. The committee is expected to provide a structured approach to translating the recommendations accepted by government into concrete proposals and actions. Government has reiterated its commitment to an inclusive and transparent constitutional review process, saying the exercise should reflect the aspirations of Ghanaians and contribute to strengthening democratic governance. The inauguration therefore marks the next stage in the process following the submission of the Constitution Review Committee’s recommendations and the government’s consideration of the proposals.

items.title: Add value to cotton before export – Trade Minister urges Ghana
items.description: Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has called for a deliberate effort to add value to Ghana’s cotton before it is exported, arguing that the country stands to gain significantly by developing a strong domestic textile and apparel value chain. According to Minister Ofosu-Adjare, Ghana and other African countries continue to lose substantial economic value by exporting raw cotton while importing processed textile products. Speaking at the launch of the Northshore Apparel manufacturing hub in Savelugu, she highlighted the need for stronger linkages between agriculture and manufacturing. “Africa’s place in that picture, however, remains far smaller than our raw material base would suggest,” Minister Ofosu-Adjare said. She noted that Africa supplies close to a tenth of the world’s traded cotton, but exports about 90 per cent of its raw cotton to Asia. “This is a clear sign of value leaving our shores before it is even spun into thread, let alone sewn into a garment,” she said. Minister Ofosu-Adjare said the situation presented an opportunity for Ghana to expand cotton production while developing industries capable of processing the crop into yarn, fabric and finished garments. She pointed to the vast agricultural potential of northern Ghana, saying the country has more than four million hectares of northern savannah zones, much of which remains uncultivated despite being suitable for cotton production. “Our country has more than 4 million hectares of northern savannah zones, much of it within which we stand remains uncultivated, even though it’s suitable for cotton cultivation,” she said. The Minister also disclosed that she had visited Bente Energies Limited at Zugali, where the company is undertaking experimental cotton cultivation. “They are cultivating cotton. And it’s doing so well,” she said. Minister Ofosu-Adjare added that the company had indicated that, if the current cultivation proved successful, it planned to expand production to more than 5,000 hectares next year. She described the development as positive news for Northshore Apparel and Ghana’s broader apparel industry, particularly as the country seeks to strengthen local sourcing of raw materials. “This is good news for Northshore and the apparel industry,” she said. The Minister said Ghana needed to move away from the traditional practice of exporting raw materials and importing finished products, stressing that greater value must be retained within the country. She cited China, Bangladesh and Vietnam as examples of developing economies that have captured significant portions of the global apparel market through deliberate investment in manufacturing and export capacity. Minister Ofosu-Adjare said Ghana could similarly position itself as a competitive player if it developed the necessary infrastructure, skills, raw material supply and market access. She said the newly commissioned Northshore Apparel facility demonstrated the potential of indigenous Ghanaian businesses to invest in large-scale manufacturing outside the traditional industrial centres of Accra and Tema. The facility, she noted, was designed to produce competitively for both local and international markets while creating employment opportunities for young people in the Northern Region. Minister Ofosu-Adjare said stronger collaboration between farmers and manufacturers would be critical to building a sustainable cotton-to-garment industry in Ghana. She stressed that producing and processing cotton locally would not only create opportunities for farmers but also support job creation, industrialisation and export growth. “Every garment that leaves this facility for a customer abroad is a step towards Ghana we are building,” she said. “A Ghana that produces, that adds value, and that exports with pride.” The Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting manufacturers, improving the ease of doing business and opening export markets through Ghana’s trade agreements. She said the ultimate goal was to build an economy that produces more, adds value to its resources and competes effectively in global markets.

items.title: The Sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln Deserve Better
items.description: W hen I was deployed at sea as a junior officer , I used milestones to track the passage of time. Each day counted toward something: a port call, when you get a break on land from the monotony at sea; the “crossing the line ceremony” when a ship crosses the equator (unfortunately, canceled at the last minute for my ship); and, eventually, the date I knew that, no matter what, I would be going home. Even on my worst days, that end point helped me stay focused on the mission and gave me something to be hopeful for. The USS Abraham Lincoln left its home port of San Diego in November and was scheduled to return home in May. That did not happen. In the middle of this month, it surpassed more than 240 consecutive days at sea—one of the longest deployments on record—and had only a brief working port call early last month, where it appears sailors did not disembark, leaving them still at sea with land in sight. The 5,000 sailors and Marines on board have been working sustained combat operations, dealing with extension after extension and unreliable access to food, basic hygiene supplies, and mail. The ship carries the name of a president who made a promise in his second inaugural address to care for people who have “borne the battle” and for their families. The treatment of those on board betrays that promise—and it is not limited to just this one ship on this one very long deployment. Rather, the crisis of the Lincoln has illuminated a pattern of callousness and cruelty toward military personnel, people who have sworn an oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States of America. They have committed to going in harm’s way, but not to being neglected or treated with disrespect by the top of their chain of command. [ Read: The timidity of America’s top generals ] The military used to understand that troops’ well-being was central to their ability to perform—and that improving the quality of life for those in the armed forces was not just a nicety, but a necessity. From 2021 to 2023, I served as acting director of force resiliency at the Department of the Navy, where I worked as part of an effort to support sailors’ and Marines’ mental health and reduce their suicide risk. Across administrations, both military leaders and career civilians have sought to foster a culture of respect throughout the armed forces. Some of that work was already ongoing during the first Trump administration: a shift toward prevention, building healthy command climates so that problems did not happen in the first place rather than being responded to only after the fact. Under the Biden administration, the Independent Review Commission on Sexual Assault in the Military produced ways to report sexual assault and harassment outside one’s chain of command, and provided independent investigators for those complaints. These efforts showed promise; sexual-assault and suicide rates have both fallen in recent years. Sailors are resilient and try to make do with whatever they have. But that does not change the fact that on the Lincoln and elsewhere, they are at the mercy of poor planning, or no planning at all. Recent reporting from The New York Times and other outlets has shown that the Lincoln’s and other ships’ logistical issues could have been anticipated as far back as February, when the main base in Bahrain was damaged by an Iranian air strike, and resupply efforts were shifted to Diego Garcia, an island 2,200 miles from where carriers operate. This information was not made public, likely to save face and for operational security. Although Department of Defense leaders have had months to find alternatives, the administration does not appear to have planned for the conflict to stretch on this long. The Navy needs more capable leaders; instead, an artificial leadership vacuum is being forced upon it from above. Throughout this year, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has been weakening the Navy’s leadership by blocking the promotion of nearly 20 admirals . He removed nine officers from the one-star-promotion list in May, and then seven more from the two-star list in July—by and large women and people of color who were selected by a board of their peers. Among those blocked from picking up a second star: Rear Admiral Amy Bauernschmidt, the first woman to command an aircraft carrier, by coincidence the USS Abraham Lincoln, which she led from 2021 to 2023. For the first time in more than a decade, no active-duty woman is likely to make admiral this year, and the subject is largely being ignored as a “woman problem” instead of being seen for the leadership crisis it is. When families of the Lincoln’s sailors started talking with reporters, their complaints were met with contempt from the top. A Pentagon spokesperson, Sean Parnell, said that “legitimate challenges of a long combat deployment are being twisted into a false narrative,” and cited his own land-based combat deployment as evidence that the sailors needed to toughen up. Hegseth blamed “the reckless & shameless ‘American’ media.” The department’s rapid-response account answered reporting on food shortages by posting, twice, that sailors had ice cream. When asked whether the Lincoln’s deployment had gone on too long, President Trump’s response was to quip “not nearly long enough.” [ Listen: The military Pete Hegseth wants ] I do not know what a junior enlisted sailor feels when they hear these comments. But there is a saying in the military that leadership sets the tone, and when the most senior leaders are flippant at best, and cruel at worst, many will understand that to be the permissible standard. The same leaders who so loudly demand that the country support the troops are not themselves doing so. And in June, this disrespect was put in writing: The Department of Defense issued a nonpublic memo on military equal opportunity and harassment that makes it easier for commanders to dismiss formal harassment complaints and retaliate against whistleblowers. Although service members do where they are told—and over the years, I have done many things while in uniform that I personally disagreed with—the respect of the commander in chief and military leaders is not supposed to be conditional. Most of their predecessors understood caring for those who go in harm’s way as a sacred obligation. T he USS Abraham Lincoln will come home . Another ship will relieve it. But homecoming is not just one day. For some sailors, the process will continue for the rest of their life. They will be expected to get back to business as normal: training, tending to the material condition of their ship, going to their new commands. They may also be moving to a new state (the Lincoln’s home port is planned to shift from San Diego to Bremerton, Washington), reconnecting with their families, and adjusting to a new pace of life. That is how the Navy operates. The Navy’s SEAL teams have a cooldown period after deployment: time for family, therapy, whatever you need to be ready for next time. The rest of the Navy has no equivalent. Whether a sailor can tend to the home front or get counseling depends entirely on her immediate command, which is to say, on her boss. And for many, the check-engine light won’t show up for years. That was true for me. The PTSD from my three deployments and some traumatic noncombat experiences didn’t really show up until two years after I had left active duty, in part because I was no longer in the middle of it. These sailors’ needs will then collide with yet another Trump-administration casualty: a weakened Veterans Affairs system. The VA eliminated nearly 30,000 positions last year. The War Horse reported on VA-medical-center policies that recommended discharging most patients from therapy after just eight sessions (far too few, according to many providers), an approach that the VA has denied adopting. The VA has lost more than 1,200 mental-health providers since the start of the administration, and demand is increasing. The department’smission statement is President Lincoln’s promise itself. The bronze plaque outside its Washington, D.C., headquarters bears his words: “ To care for him who shall have borne the battle and for his widow, and his orphan. ” That’s not a promise the government is living up to today.

items.title: Du pâturage aux étals, le parcours difficile de la viande au Mali
items.description: © Internet La 6ᵉ Assemblée générale ordinaire de l’Interprofession de la filière bétail-viande du Mali (IFBV-Mali) s’est tenue jeudi 27 août 2026 au Mémorial Modibo Keïta de Bamako. Elle a porté sur les difficultés de la filière et les moyens d’améliorer l’approvisionnement des marchés. À Bamako comme dans plusieurs régions du pays, la question de la viande dépasse le simple prix affiché chez le boucher. Derrière un kilogramme vendu entre 3 500 et 4 000 francs CFA dans certaines localités se trouve une chaîne fragilisée par l’insécurité, les difficultés de transport et la réduction de l’offre. C’est dans ce contexte que l’IFBV-Mali a réuni les principales familles professionnelles du secteur : éleveurs, transformateurs, marchands et transporteurs de bétail. Pour son président, Mamoudou Abdoulaye Diallo, la participation des délégations régionales, malgré la saison des pluies, témoigne de l’engagement des acteurs. « Cette mobilisation de toutes les régions du Mali et du District de Bamako montre vraiment la vitalité de notre organisation », estime-t-il. L’assemblée intervient alors que l’insécurité perturbe les déplacements des éleveurs et des animaux, le fonctionnement des marchés à bétail et les circuits traditionnels d’approvisionnement. Dans la région de Bandiagara, Amadou Traoré, président des bouchers, décrit une activité profondément ralentie. Il y a encore quelques années, les professionnels pouvaient se déplacer dans plusieurs villes pour acheter du bétail. Aujourd’hui, ces mouvements sont devenus plus difficiles et la baisse de l’offre se mesure jusque dans les abattoirs. « Maintenant, on n’abat plus que trois vaches, alors qu’auparavant, on pouvait en abattre jusqu’à 20, sans compter les moutons et les chèvres », témoigne-t-il. Plusieurs bouchers auraient également cessé leur activité. La région dispose désormais d’un abattoir, mais celui-ci ne répond pas suffisamment aux besoins des professionnels, selon Amadou Traoré. Le manque d’équipements de conservation complique également la commercialisation de la viande. À Bandiagara, le problème commence bien avant l’arrivée de la viande sur les étals. Boubacar Koïta, commerçant de bétail, situe l’un des principaux points de blocage sur l’axe Bandiagara-Fatoma, important pour l’approvisionnement de la région. « Nous, les commerçants, nous partions avec nos bouchers et chacun trouvait sa part, mais cette chaîne a été coupée », explique-t-il. Sa sécurisation permettrait, selon lui, de faciliter le ravitaillement de la ville, où le kilogramme de viande est vendu entre 3 500 et 4 000 francs CFA. Le constat est similaire dans la région de Mopti. Alboucar Bocoum, secrétaire général de l’Union régionale des marchands de bétail, rappelle que cette zone est traditionnellement considérée comme un important bassin d’élevage. Certains éleveurs ont cependant quitté leurs espaces habituels, des animaux ont été enlevés et les déplacements vers les marchés sont devenus plus risqués. Le rapprochement des marchés à bétail ne suffit donc pas lorsque les éleveurs et les commerçants hésitent à prendre la route. « Quand le marché n’est pas suffisamment approvisionné, le peu qui s’y présente coûte vraiment cher », résume-t-il. Une hausse saisonnière Face à l’augmentation du prix de la viande, le président de l’IFBV-Mali appelle toutefois les consommateurs à ne pas céder à l’inquiétude. Selon Mamoudou Abdoulaye Diallo, cette hausse présente aussi un caractère saisonnier. L’hivernage et les mouvements de transhumance éloignent temporairement une partie du cheptel des grands centres urbains. Avec la fin progressive de cette période, les animaux devraient se rapprocher des centres de consommation et améliorer l’approvisionnement des marchés. L’interprofession affirme que ses membres poursuivent les activités pastorales et d’embouche afin de renforcer l’offre. Pour les professionnels, cette réponse restera cependant insuffisante sans une amélioration de la sécurité sur les axes de circulation. Abdoulaye Buimayara, représentant de la région de Douentza, décrit des difficultés qui commencent dans les zones de production et se prolongent jusqu’à Bamako. L’insuffisance des moyens de transport et les contraintes sur les routes compliquent l’activité. Dans sa région, le kilogramme de viande peut atteindre 4 000 francs CFA. Pour Mahamadou Doucouré, secrétaire général de l’IFBV-Mali, les difficultés doivent être traitées à l’échelle de toute la chaîne. « Tout commence au niveau des éleveurs avant d’arriver aux autres », souligne-t-il. Les différentes familles professionnelles doivent donc agir ensemble pour améliorer l’approvisionnement des consommateurs. Cette volonté de travailler collectivement constitue l’un des objectifs de l’Assemblée générale. Le président de l’interprofession souhaite l’instauration d’un cadre régulier de concertation avec les pouvoirs publics, afin que les professionnels puissent faire remonter leurs difficultés et participer à la recherche de solutions. L’IFBV-Mali entend également renforcer les familles professionnelles et mieux valoriser leurs productions. L’opérationnalisation du label « Mali Sogo », enregistré comme marque collective auprès de l’Organisation africaine de la propriété intellectuelle, figure parmi les perspectives. Cette certification doit garantir l’origine et la traçabilité de la viande rouge malienne et renforcer son positionnement sur les marchés. Le représentant du ministre de l’Élevage et de la Pêche a salué la régularité des sessions et appelé les acteurs à relever les faiblesses de la filière. L’objectif est de garantir une production plus régulière, d’améliorer l’approvisionnement et de contribuer aux différentes dimensions de la sécurité alimentaire. Pour les professionnels, l’enjeu est de permettre au bétail de circuler, aux marchés d’être régulièrement approvisionnés et à la viande de redevenir plus accessible. Restaurer cette chaîne passe d’abord par la sécurité, la concertation et la circulation des animaux entre les zones d’élevage et les centres de consommation. Salimata Wagué

items.title: Koosin/Nouna Jeunesse Vacances Art et Culture : Les valeurs endogènes mises à l’honneur lors d’une soirée culturelle
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-CULTURE-JEUNESSE Koosin/Nouna Jeunesse Vacances Art et Culture : Les valeurs endogènes mises à l’honneur lors d’une soirée culturelle Nouna, 27 août 2026 (AIB)-L’Association Espace Culturel Yelen de Nouna a organisé le jeudi 27 août 2026, une soirée culturelle consacrée à la promotion des valeurs endogènes et de la créativité locale, à l’occasion de la deuxième édition de « Nouna Jeunesse Vacances Art et Culture ». Placée sous la présidence du Haut-commissaire de la province de la Koosin, Noufo Dembélé et le patronage du ministre de la Construction de la Patrie, Mikaïlou Sidibé, l’activité a eu pour invité d’honneur Abdina Koeta. La soirée a été marquée par des activités artistiques, culturelles et citoyennes. Après l’intervention du président de l’Association Espace Culturel Yelen, Moussa Sangaré, le président du comité d’organisation, Issa Mada Dama, a souhaité la bienvenue aux invités et aux participants. Sur le site, des produits et mets locaux étaient exposés en vue de leur commercialisation et de la promotion des savoir-faire, des tenues et de la gastronomie traditionnels. Les prestations artistiques ont notamment été marquées par une démonstration de danses traditionnelles exécutées par la troupe de Sobon, mettant en valeur la culture marka. Le public a également apprécié la prestation de la chanteuse Aïcha Koné, artiste originaire de Nouna, qui a notamment interprété un titre consacré à la paix et au vivre-ensemble. La créativité locale a aussi été mise en avant à travers un défilé de mode animé par deux professionnels de la couture basés à Nouna, Levis Couture et Maël Style, qui ont présenté leurs différentes créations au public. La soirée a également servi de cadre à une communication sur les différents volets des initiatives présidentielles. Le point focal, Kassoum Dramé, a expliqué aux participants les domaines concernés par ces initiatives, invitant la jeunesse à s’engager davantage dans la citoyenneté et le développement de la communauté. En fin de soirée, des prix ont été décernés à un jeune homme et une jeune femme, désignés comme les plus stylés de la soirée. Le président de l’Association Espace Culturel Yelen, a souligné que la jeunesse ne se limite pas à une tranche d’âge. « Le jeune n’est pas seulement celui qui a 20 ans, mais aussi celui qui, même à 60 ans, participe activement au développement », a déclaré Moussa Sangaré. Agence d’information du Burkina ID/AC/HB/OO

items.title: Economie : Le ministre Patoki salue la gestion rigoureuse des ressources prônée par le Président du Conseil
items.description: Lomé, 28 août (ATOP) – Le ministre de l’Economie et de la Veille stratégique, Patoki Badanam, a salué, le vendredi 28 août à Lomé, la vision du Président du Conseil en matière de gouvernance et de gestion des ressources publiques et privées, à l’occasion du lancement officiel des activités du Conseil national de la comptabilité (CNC). « Je rends un hommage mérité au Président du Conseil dont la vision et les orientations donnent une impulsion renouvelée à la modernisation de notre économie et au renforcement des conditions permettant à chaque acteur économique de contribuer pleinement au développement de notre pays », a déclaré M. Patoki. Le ministre s’est notamment référé aux orientations énoncées par le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, lors de son adresse au Parlement, le 3 décembre 2015. A cette occasion, le Président du Conseil avait insisté, selon le ministre, sur la nécessité d’une nouvelle approche de la gouvernance fondée sur la clarté des engagements, la redevabilité et la responsabilité partagée. Il avait également mis l’accent sur la définition d’objectifs précis, leur suivi et leur évaluation, ainsi que sur la nécessité d’une gestion fondée sur des résultats vérifiables. Cette vision, a expliqué M. Patoki, appelle à la consolidation d’institutions fortes et à la mise en place de mécanismes de gouvernance modernes, accompagnés d’outils capables de garantir la transparence, la fiabilité de l’information et une gestion rigoureuse des ressources publiques et privées. « C’est dans cette dynamique que s’inscrit le lancement officiel des activités du CNC, dont la mission est jugée essentielle pour renforcer la crédibilité du système d’information financière au Togo, promouvoir les bonnes pratiques comptables et contribuer à l’instauration d’un environnement économique plus transparent, attractif et performant », a-t-il. La comptabilité, un outil de gouvernance Le ministre Patoki rend hommage au Président du Conseil Le ministre Patoki a rappelé que la comptabilité ne saurait être réduite à une simple technique d’enregistrement et de présentation des opérations financières. Elle constitue également, a-t-il souligné, un véritable langage de transparence, de gouvernance et de confiance. « Dans un environnement économique sous-régional marqué par les exigences de l’OHADA, de l’UMOA et des investisseurs internationaux, la qualité de l’information comptable devient un levier stratégique pour renforcer la transparence dans la gestion économique », a-t-il relevé. A travers la mise en place du CNC, a-t-il poursuivi, le gouvernement entend notamment contribuer à l’amélioration de la qualité de l’information financière, faciliter l’attractivité des investissements et garantir une meilleure comparabilité ainsi qu’une plus grande fiabilité des données financières. M. Patoki a fait savoir que le lancement du CNC apparaît ainsi comme une étape importante dans le renforcement du dispositif national de gouvernance comptable et financière, au service d’une économie plus transparente et davantage tournée vers la performance. ATOP/DHK/AJA/BV

items.title: Why Barcelona did not honour Spain’s World Cup-winning players
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Barcelona shelved plans to honour the club’s eight Spain internationals who helped the country win the World Cup, following a dispute over the treatment of a fan carrying a Catalan pro-independence flag. The tribute was initially scheduled for Barcelona’s first La Liga home game of the season against Athletic Bilbao. However, the club decided against the ceremony after a Barcelona supporter had his estelada, a flag associated with Catalonia’s independence movement, confiscated by police before the team’s away fixture against Elche. The incident escalated after the young supporter reportedly confronted the officers and was struck with batons before being detained. Barcelona subsequently criticised the police action and expressed regret over the confiscation of the flag. The club described the estelada as “a legally endorsed symbol”, arguing that displaying it was “a legitimate exercise of freedom of expression.” Barcelona added that the flag’s display “cannot in itself be considered an incitement to hatred or violence.” The club also said the manner in which the supporter was detained was disproportionate, stating that “the use of force lacked the necessary justification and appropriateness.” The controversy took on a wider political dimension ahead of Thursday’s match, with a Catalan organisation distributing about 10,000 estelada flags to supporters outside Camp Nou. Thousands of fans later raised the flags during Barcelona’s anthem, while some supporters also marched near the stadium carrying the pro-independence symbols. Barcelona president Joan Laporta described the display as a peaceful “act of exaltation of the estelada”, saying it reflected Catalans’ right to freedom of expression. Explaining why the tribute to the Spain players was dropped, Laporta said it was “not the most appropriate moment”, stressing that “soccer must unite, not generate confrontations.” Barcelona had been expected to celebrate its eight World Cup winners, the highest number of players from any club in the Spain squad. The players are Joan García, Eric García, Pedri, Pau Cubarsí, Gavi, Rodri, Dani Olmo and Lamine Yamal. While other Spanish clubs honoured their World Cup-winning players in ceremonies supported by the Spanish football federation, Barcelona opted to avoid a similar celebration amid the controversy. Despite the off-field tensions, Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao 2-0 in the league fixture courtsey of goals from Raphinha and Fermin Lopez. The post Why Barcelona did not honour Spain’s World Cup-winning players appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Economie : Les activités du Conseil national de la comptabilité lancées
items.description: Lomé, 28 août (ATOP) – Le ministre de l’Economie et de la Veille stratégique, Patoki Badanam a lancé, le vendredi 28 août à Lomé, les activités du Conseil national de la comptabilité (CNC), une structure destinée à renforcer la qualité et la transparence de la gouvernance économique au Togo. Le CNC a pour mission d’émettre des avis préalables sur tout projet de réglementation d’ordre comptable en particulier sur les aspects comptables des activités économiques et financières. Il va soumettre au Conseil comptable ouest-africain toute proposition relative à l’exploitation des comptes, soit dans l’intérêt des entreprises, soit dans l’établissement des statistiques nationales des budgets et des comptes économiques de l’Etat. Le CNC doit, aussi, formuler à l’intention du Conseil comptable ouest-africain des avis et recommandations sur toute question relative à l’application d’une norme comptable ; assurer la coordination et la synthèse des recherches théoriques et méthodologiques de comptabilité. Le Conseil sera aussi chargé de collecter, centraliser et diffuser toute information et documentation relative à l’enseignement de la comptabilité, à l’organisation et la tenue des comptes. Des participants Le CNC doit, également, réaliser toutes les études à la demande du Conseil comptable ouest-africain ; et faire de la comptabilité un outil stratégique de pilotage économique au service du développement durable et de la bonne gouvernance. Le ministre Patoki a demandé aux neuf membres du Conseil d’inscrire leur vision dans les priorités du gouvernement, celles de rendre le secteur privé plus viable et davantage créateur de richesses et d’emplois. « J’insiste véritablement sur ce qui est important pour la matière elle-même et sur ce que vous devez faire. L’éthique, la discipline et l’excellence professionnelle doivent être au-devant de tout. Vous êtes appelés à faire preuve de rigueur dans vos décisions, à défendre les meilleures pratiques et à promouvoir l’intérêt général dans toutes vos recommandations », a-t-il signifié. Le ministre les a exhortés à développer une franche collaboration entre eux, à tous les niveaux, à cultiver dans l’accomplissement de leur mission, l’esprit du dialogue d’intégrité et de responsabilité partagée. « Nous devons faire de ce Conseil, un organe dynamique, crédible et proche des professionnels, des entreprises, des administrations publiques et de tous les utilisateurs de l’information comptable. Le chemin qui s’ouvre devant nous aujourd’hui est certes exigeant, mais il est également porteur de grandes perspectives pour notre pays en matière de pratique comptable », a indiqué le président du CNC, Emegnimo Elonyo Apollinaire. Il a invité ses collaborateurs à s’engager véritablement pour cette nouvelle ère en faveur d’une comptabilité de qualité et de transparence dans le pays. ATOP/DHK/BA/BV

items.title: Koulikoro : 9 morts sur les routes en juillet
items.description: a Koulikoro, les accidents de la circulation ont fait neuf morts et 266 blesses en juillet 2026. items.title: Man Utd new signing Baleba sidelined for three weeks
items.description: Michael Carrick said Carlos Baleba will be unable to make his Manchester United debut for around three weeks due to an ankle injury, but is excited by the Cameroonian’s “massive potential”. Baleba’s £70 million ($95 million) move from Brighton further bolstered Carrick’s midfield options after the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. But United could have to wait until October to see Baleba in action as he faces a race against time to return before a three-week international break next month. “He’s got a little ankle issue, so maybe a couple of weeks or so, maybe three weeks. We’ll see but we knew that before, so it’s no major issue but it’ll be great to have him back when we can,” Carrick told his pre-match press conference ahead of Ipswich’s visit on Sunday. “We’re delighted to have Carlos. I think (he has) huge potential, massive potential. I think he’s a really exciting signing for us. “I think the quality that he has, the attributes that he has that offsets a little bit of the balance of the group that we’ve got. Different strengths, different combinations.” Carrick was rewarded with the United job on a permanent basis after guiding the Red Devils to third in the Premier League last season during an interim spell in charge. However, the new campaign got off to the worst possible start for Carrick with a 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull last weekend. Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez all started that match on the bench after missing most of pre-season due to their participation in the latter stages of the World Cup. Carrick confirmed all three could return to the starting line-up, but Amad Diallo will miss out once more through injury. AFP The post Man Utd new signing Baleba sidelined for three weeks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Couverture médiatique des élections en Guinée : « Aucun parti politique, aucun candidat indépendant n’a saisi la HAC à l’effet de porter une plainte », dit Boubacar Yacine Diallo
items.description: Le président de la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC), Boubacar Yacine Diallo, a animé une conférence de presse ce vendredi 28 août 2026 au siège de l’institution. Objectif : présenter le rapport général sur la régulation des campagnes médiatiques des trois scrutins — présidentiel, législatif et communal — tenus respectivement le 28 décembre 2025 et le 31 mai 2026. Ce document de 207 pages aborde tous les aspects liés à la couverture médiatique de ces rendez-vous électoraux dans les sept régions administratives ainsi que dans les treize communes de Conakry. « Le rapport préliminaire qui a été élaboré avait plus de 500 pages. Si vous le désirez, nous pourrions vous le transférer sous forme de PDF pour votre usage. Nous ne pouvions pas publier 500 pages d’un rapport, ce serait fastidieux pour le lecteur. Donc, c’est en réalité une synthèse du rapport qui avoisine ou dépasse les cinq centaines. Ce rapport, donc, c’est la photographie de la couverture médiatique des trois campagnes. Et je voudrais déjà saluer le professionnalisme, l’esprit de responsabilité qui ont caractérisé les professionnels et médias, tous si fort confondus : l’audiovisuel, la presse en ligne, la presse écrite, et même quelques jeunes qui ont des sites qui ne sont pas reconnus, mais qui exercent. La preuve, c’est que nous n’avons reçu aucune plainte de qui que ce soit contre un journaliste ou contre un média ou contre un correspondant de la presse étrangère, ce qui est rare. Je voudrais donc saluer votre travail, saluer votre esprit de responsabilité, saluer également la synergie des radios qui a été organisée par l’URTELGUI et qui a permis, dès le soir du jour du scrutin, de publier les procès-verbaux dûment signés et affichés. Cela aussi est très rare. Je pense que la Guinée est le seul pays qui a une synergie des radios, qui travaille pendant des heures, parfois pendant des jours pour couvrir une campagne électorale et diffuser dès après les résultats des procès-verbaux, parce que la totalisation est interdite pour les médias. Elle n’appartient qu’à la DGE, comme entité compétente pour diffuser des résultats provisoires, et derrière, à la Cour suprême pour les élections nationales et aux tribunaux pour les élections locales. Donc, le premier mérite vous revient. La HAC vous en félicite et vous encourage à poursuivre ce débat, à poursuivre cette dynamique », a déclaré Boubacar Yacine Diallo. Selon le président de la HAC, plusieurs innovations ont été apportées lors de ces scrutins, ce qui a d’ailleurs favorisé l’obtention des résultats escomptés. « La première innovation consistait à associer des radios privées parce que les élections communales et les élections législatives, dans leur volet uninominal et plurinominal, nous ont mis face à un défi. C’est celui de la distribution équitable des temps d’antenne et nous avons été inspirés pour utiliser les radios privées sur des sujets qui concernent la vie et le développement des circonscriptions. Je voudrais donc saluer ce partenariat et j’espère que celui-ci sera étendu à d’autres radios et à d’autres télévisions et, pourquoi pas, à d’autres médias de presse écrite et de presse en ligne. La deuxième innovation, c’est d’avoir associé les radios rurales. Les 33 radios rurales ont été mises à contribution pour donner la parole aux candidats dans chacune de ces circonscriptions. Et cela aussi est une expérience unique parce que, dans la plupart des pays, on nous dit que les radios rurales ne doivent pas faire de la politique. Mais je dis, lorsqu’on parle du développement d’une localité, lorsqu’on concourt pour gérer la commune, est-ce que la radio rurale peut se soustraire à une telle activité ? La réponse est non. Donc, les radios rurales ont servi de relais à la campagne médiatique pour les élections locales. Et nous avons bénéficié de la totale compréhension de la direction de la radio rurale. Je voudrais la remercier, et les directeurs des stations ont fait un travail professionnel irréprochable. Qu’ils en soient, eux aussi, remerciés. L’autre innovation que nous avons pu faire, c’est celle de découvrir des journalistes à l’intérieur du pays. Vous savez, jusqu’à récemment, nous n’avions que des points focaux dans les sept régions administratives. Ces points focaux, ce n’est pas l’invention de notre collège, nous les avons trouvés sur place. Ce que nous avons fait, c’est que nous avons contribué à dynamiser leur représentativité sur le terrain. Ils sont plus visibles que par le passé, ils sont plus actifs que par le passé. Mais les élections communales nous ont fait découvrir la qualité du superviseur. Donc, nous avons désigné un superviseur par circonscription. Une circonscription équivalente à une préfecture. Donc, dans chacune de nos préfectures, nous avons désigné un superviseur qui jouait exactement le rôle que notre comité de suivi de la campagne a prévu. Donc, ces jeunes journalistes que nous découvrions à peine ont su faire notre travail à notre place, de Conakry à Yomou, de Lélouma à Forécariah. Et aucun parti politique, aucun candidat indépendant n’a saisi la HAC à l’effet de porter une plainte. Au contraire, nous avons reçu des félicitations de beaucoup de candidats envers ces jeunes journalistes que nous avons découverts et qui sont devenus les superviseurs de la HAC à l’intérieur du pays. Je voudrais donc leur dire merci. Et d’ailleurs, nous en avons tiré une conséquence heureuse. Donc, nous les avons désignés comme les superviseurs permanents de la HAC dans chacune des préfectures et dans les 13 communes de Conakry », a révélé Boubacar Yacine Diallo, qui, de passage, a remercié les autorités pour avoir mis les moyens nécessaires à la disposition de la HAC, permettant ainsi à son équipe d’accomplir son travail. Lébêré Baldé L’article Couverture médiatique des élections en Guinée : « Aucun parti politique, aucun candidat indépendant n’a saisi la HAC à l’effet de porter une plainte », dit Boubacar Yacine Diallo est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d’origine camerounaise
items.description: © DR Jugés coupables d'avoir fourni du soutien financier et logistique pour la fabrication et l'utilisation des engins explosifs improvisés au Cameroun, ils n'échappent pas à de lourdes peines. Ils écopent des peines allant de cinq à 15 ans de prison ferme. Francis Chenyi âgé de 52 ans, Lah Nestor Langmi, 49 ans tombent sous le coup d'une condamnation de 15 ans de prison chacun. Tandis que Claude Ngenevu Chi, 43 ans, doit purger 63 mois de prison correspondant à un peu plus de 5 ans. Après avoir purgé les différentes peines, les trois condamnés seront soumis chacun à trois ans de liberté surveillée. Ainsi a décidé le tribunal fédéral de Kansas City dans le Missouri. Il est reproché aux trois ressortissants camerounais d'avoir appartenu à un réseau de financement et de fourniture de la logistique au profit des combattants séparatistes qui opèrent dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest. Ils ont exercé des missions de coordination des opérations de fabrication des engins explosifs improvisés ainsi que de la formation des personnes en vue de leur utilisation, apprend-on de sources médiatiques. Des mêmes sources, cette coordination s'étend aussi à des attaques à l'aide de ces explosifs en ciblant plusieurs villes du Nord-Ouest et à proximité du stade devant accueillir la CAN 2021 dans la région du Sud-Ouest. Aussi, la justice reproche à ces trois hommes d'avoir coordonné des opérations de transfert des fonds des États-Unis vers le Cameroun. Des fonds qui ont servi à réaliser des projets d'attaques évoqués plus haut. De manière individuelle, la justice reproche à Langmi d'avoir participé à la coordination des opérations d'enlèvements dont celui du chef traditionnel Fonmbam Aforteka et celui du cardinal Christian Tumi de regrettée mémoire. Pour la commission de ces faits, Chenyi aurait fourni une contribution financière. Ce sont ainsi trois financiers de plus de la crise anglophone qui sont condamnés par la justice américaine dans le cadre du règlement de la crise. Depuis quelques années, d'autres Camerounais ont écopé des condamnations à des peines diverses presque pour les mêmes motifs. Che Ernest Banhary et Edith Ngang ont écopé de quatre ans de prison ferme. En 2024, une trentaine de leaders séparatistes ont été traduits devant les juridictions américaines à la suite de plusieurs plaintes déposées par le cabinet Me Nsahlai à la demande de l'Etat camerounais. Les États-Unis se sont engagés à poursuivre juger et condamner ces hommes suspectés d'avoir participé à financer ou à commettre des actes terroristes sur le territoire camerounais. Cet article Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d'origine camerounaise est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
